why: A's judgment is backed by measurement where B's is borrowed: A proved prompt caching on the OpenAI side buys nothing here (automatic prefix cache already hits) and instead measured the real lever — Anthropic cache_control, 6,889 prefix tokens read back, 89% off a reflection turn — while B shipped prompt_cache_key=$feature into the base migration on ROUTER.md numbers it admits it never re-measured, and cited a Claude-over-Responses figure that doesn't apply to this app's /v1/messages path. A also keeps behaviour-changing model remaps on reviewable branches with live 404 evidence, whereas B folds a different Claude and a different reviewer model into the migration branch itself, which is where 'keep behaviour intact' is supposed to hold; B's better ideas (cross-vendor fallbacks for an unattended GPU pipeline, a cheap model for the ~500-call novelty check) are real CTO thinking but unbuilt and unmeasured.
A_best: Measured negative results — prompt_cache_key, Flex and provider_timeout each tested and rejected with specific evidence (two gpt-4o arms both caching 3,840 tokens; flex=no in the catalog; a 504 the backoff decorator won't retry) — plus the one caching win that is real for this app, Claude cache_control with live token counts and a stated 1.25x write cost and break-even.
B_best: The improvement that neither validation nor A reached for: Router fallbacks as the answer to this pipeline's actual failure mode — an unbounded backoff on rate limits and a bare 5xx that makes do_idea discard hours of GPU work — correctly scoped as /v1/responses-only and honestly marked unmeasured on real outages.
A_worst: Nothing on resilience. For an hours-long unattended batch job where one 503 throws away an idea's GPU time, A listed fallbacks as 'reviewed' and then produced no item on them, and its only resilience reasoning is a rejection of provider_timeout — so the migration leaves the app's worst operational gap untouched.
B_worst: m5: prompt_cache_key shipped into the migration branch with its benefit asserted from ROUTER.md's 9k-token sample rather than this app, when A's direct measurement shows OpenAI's automatic prefix cache already captures that gain and the quoted Claude-caching figure belongs to a Responses path this app never uses — a cost claim in the default-ship commit that is probably wrong.
